blocks.label: BAR HEIGHTS: HOW MUCH WATER STAYS?

slides.teaser: The problem, as rain on a wall
slides.title: Rain on a wall
slides.scene: Rain falls on a row of walls of different heights. Water collects in the dips between them and spills over the lower side.

blocks.text: How many squares of water stay on top?

slides.title: LeetCode 42
slides.lead: Given bar heights, return how much water is trapped after rain.

blocks.text: Up to 20,000 bars, each up to 100,000 tall.

slides.try_first: Work out the water above each of the 6 bars by hand.

slides.teaser: Hint 1: one bar at a time
slides.title: Water above one bar
slides.lead: Water above a bar = the lower of the tallest walls on its two sides, minus the bar.

slides.title: Don't rescan
slides.lead: Scanning both sides for every bar is O(n²). Each tallest wall can be carried along instead.

blocks.text: Two arrays make it O(n) time, but O(n) space too.

slides.title: Two walkers
slides.lead: Start at both ends. Settle the lower side: its own tallest wall decides its water.

slides.title: Why lower is safe
slides.lead: The other side holds a bar at least as tall, so the lower side's own wall is the limit.

blocks.label: AT THE 0 ON THE RIGHT
blocks.text: rightMax is 2 and the left end is 3, so the water is [[2 − 0 = 2]], whatever lies between.

slides.pattern: Two pointers that settle the lower side, using that side's tallest wall.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.note: Same walls, same two walkers, a new question.

blog.summary: Water above each bar is the lower of the tallest walls on its two sides, minus the bar.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (the LeetCode examples, one or two bars, rising, falling, flat, very tall walls) and random rows of up to 14 bars, plus one row of 3,000 bars
blog.tested_against: a brute force that finds both tallest walls for every bar
blog.tested_extra: The water per bar, the total and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: LeetCode 42 Trapping Rain Water solved with hints: two walkers settle the lower side in O(n) time and O(1) space.
lines: Water above a bar = min(tallest left, tallest right) − bar.
The trap: settle the taller side and 3 0 1 4 0 2 gives 5 instead of 7.
